items.title: Manny Albam interviewed by Monk Rowe, Tarrytown, New York, October 31, 1998
items.q: I was on the subway once and Fletcher Henderson was in the subway writing out parts.

ctx.x: Did you have a book or something that you learned about transpositions or you just figured it out?

No I figured it out from playing stock arrangements. One of the things about stock arrangements is they were awful. The voicing was awful. I used to take them home and re-voice them for saxophone. That was the beginning of it. Now I never knew about scores in the beginning. I used to write the first trumpet part out and I would lay it aside and then look at it and write the second part out and then say well my alto is going to have to do something, and I’d write an alto part and before I knew it my bedroom was…
Yeah, like wow. A score pad.
